mul penei is a fixed relational expression on which the ASV spends the single word front: the in is el's and the of is the rectum's, so rule 30's one-English-word condition is met and the two morphemes share one unit. Rule 22 does not reach penei, since mul and penei are not one element repeated but the parts of one idiom, which rule 30 states in terms. Headed on the relational noun penei.

review_notes: Chapter reconciliation: mul penei is now one fused unit (rule 30) in place of mul aligned to front beside penei unrepresented (rule 22). The verse's original reasoning counted the in and the of as English spent on the expression, but the alignment gives the in to el and the of to the rectum, so only front is spent on the pair.

Fusing the whole el mul penei as a compound preposition in front of, under rule 19's rider, was available; rule 2 keeps el's in and the rectum's of as pieces that remain meaningful, so only mul and penei are joined.
Head on mul rather than penei is the choice made; the chapter's lifnei units head on penei, and that reading remains defensible here.
